ea0a0ecbcbb5cda7afb446355e90cc4deb3afdb3: The Laax ski area, with its 176 km of runs, offers something for every type of skier: big enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 29 lifts make it easy to string together runs without long queues. Laax's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. When it comes to snow, Laax is in a strong position with its highest point at 3018 m – even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well until April. The village at 1020 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from the start of mid-December. A stay in Laax is clearly expensive: €92 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence – but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Laax delivers on its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit the majority of skiers without disappointing.

Hochfügen's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Hochfügen's altitude (1480 m at the base, 2378 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.
